stages.name: Inoculation
stages.desc: Attach broodlac to host-tree twigs. Choose young shoots 6–8 mm diameter.

stages.name: Crawlers emerge
stages.desc: Tiny first-instar crawlers emerge from broodlac and settle on tender twigs.

stages.name: Development
stages.desc: Lac insects feed, encrust, and form the sticklac layer. Avoid disturbing.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.desc: Cut inoculated twigs when 75% of insects have matured. Retain some for next cycle.

notes: Suitable host: Ber (Ziziphus mauritiana) and Flemingia semialata.
Harvested sticklac should be processed within 3 days to avoid insect emergence.
Typical yield: 3–6 kg sticklac per kg broodlac on Ber (ICAR-IINRG estimate).
risks: Avoid heavy rain or frost during inoculation.
Heat > 38°C in April may reduce survival.

stages.name: Inoculation
stages.desc: Monsoon inoculation on freshly grown twigs.

stages.name: Development
stages.desc: Main growth during monsoon. Heavy rain is the primary risk.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.desc: Post-monsoon harvest. Sticklac dries quickly in cooler weather.

notes: Katki season coincides with the monsoon — excess rainfall is the main risk.
Use shade net if rainfall > 300 mm/month during development.
Typical yield: 2–4 kg sticklac per kg broodlac (lower due to monsoon losses).
risks: Heavy rain (>400 mm/month) washes broodlac off twigs.
Monitor for fungal infection in humid conditions.

stages.name: Inoculation
stages.desc: Post-kharif harvest inoculation on Kusum twigs.

stages.name: Winter growth
stages.desc: Slow development during cool season. Cold tolerance is a key advantage of Kusmi strain.

stages.name: Spring flush
stages.desc: Accelerated growth as temperatures rise. Check for parasite infestation.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.desc: Harvest before rains start. Highest quality sticklac from Kusmi Jethwi.

notes: Kusmi strain preferred on Kusum (Schleichera oleosa) — best quality resin.
Longest duration crop — requires sustained attention over 6–7 months.
Premium price commanded by Kusmi shellac in export markets.
risks: Late frost below 5°C can kill broodlac on exposed twigs.
Ensure harvest before June monsoon onset.

stages.name: Inoculation
stages.desc: Pre-monsoon inoculation on Kusum. Timing is critical — before heavy rains.

stages.name: Monsoon growth
stages.desc: Development during monsoon. Kusum's dense canopy provides partial protection.

stages.name: Post-monsoon
stages.desc: Maturation in cooler, drier weather. Optimal final development period.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.desc: Winter harvest. Aghani sticklac has high resin content.

notes: Aghani is the single most important lac crop in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh.
Kusum tree availability determines scale — requires established trees.
Typical yield: 5–9 kg sticklac per kg broodlac on mature Kusum.
risks: Heavy monsoon (>500 mm total) risks washout during June–August.
Ensure adequate broodlac supply from Jethwi harvest.
